# SOP-P1-L2-03 First-article inspection - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03

Purpose
1. This procedure defines the first-article inspection (FAI) workflow for ring-rolling production on line P1-L2. It documents required preconditions, inspection steps, acceptance rationale, records to retain, and sign-off criteria for release of the first-part lot into routine production.

Scope
2. Applies to first-part submission for any new ring geometry, new material lot, or after process change on equipment EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03. Maintenance requirements referenced are in MM-P1-L2-IH02, MM-P1-L2-RR01, and MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1.

Preconditions
3. Equipment condition
   3.1 Verify EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, and EQ-P1-L2-HT03 are available and have passed the most recent maintenance release per MM-P1-L2-RR01 and MM-P1-L2-IH02.  
   3.2 Confirm the lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is CFW-LUB-961 and that the installed reservoir and distribution lines contain that lubricant. Cross-check stock label with machine nameplate and maintenance records.

4. Material and thermal
   4.1 Confirm material certificate accompanies the billet and that chemical and mechanical attributes meet purchase order requirements.  
   4.2 Confirm the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 1230 °C and that the billet reaches and is held at that target prior to roll engagement. Record the achieved temperature in the process log.

5. Setup verification
   5.1 Verify tooling and mandrel geometry match the part print and setup sheet.  
   5.2 Verify dimensional gauges and measurement instruments are calibrated and within calibration period. Refer to MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1 for tooling changeover and quick-verify checks.

PPE
6. Required personal protective equipment for personnel involved in the FAI:
   6.1 Heat-resistant gloves and sleeves.  
   6.2 Face shield with heat-filtering visor.  
   6.3 Hearing protection.  
   6.4 Safety footwear with metatarsal protection.  
   6.5 Flame-retardant apron for handling hot billets.  
   Note: Additional PPE directed by the plant safety officer must be worn as required.

Procedure — Inspection steps
7. Preparation
   7.1 Ensure all preconditions in section 3 through 5 are satisfied and documented.  
   7.2 Perform a preheat cycle on EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and confirm that the temperature control readout stabilizes at the target value stated in section 4.2 before introducing the production billet.

8. First part processing
   8.1 Load the first billet following standard handling and hoist procedures. Monitor, log, and confirm the billet temperature reaches the target specified in section 4.2 prior to transfer to EQ-P1-L2-RR01.  
   8.2 Observe and verify lubricant flow and distribution on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 at the start of ring engagement; confirm CFW-LUB-961 supply pressure and filter condition per visual and gauge checks. If the lubricant identity or appearance differs from expected, stop and tag the machine out until resolved.

9. Dimensional verification
   9.1 After ring rolling, allow the ring to reach a safe handling temperature per plant safety directions, then perform the full dimensional inspection per the part drawing: concentricity, wall thickness profile, outside diameter, inside diameter and finish. Record all readings in the FAI data sheet.  
   9.2 Compare measured values to the drawing tolerances and document any deviations and the corrective action taken. For borderline outcomes, use the measurement method traceable to the instrument calibration log.

10. Metallurgical and surface checks
   10.1 Perform visual surface inspection for laps, seams, and surface oxide. Document surface condition with photographs and notes.  
   10.2 Remove representative samples for hardness and microstructure checks as specified by the engineering test plan. Attach test reports to the FAI package.

11. Process parameter review
   11.1 Review process logs from EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and EQ-P1-L2-RR01 for the first-part cycle. Ensure the recorded billet temperature matches the target in section 4.2 and that no excursion or equipment fault alarms were present.  
   11.2 Record machine settings, tooling identifiers, lubricant batch, and any online adjustments.

12. Final disposition
   12.1 If all dimensional, metallurgical, and surface criteria are met, sign off on the FAI and approve the lot for release into production.  
   12.2 If any nonconformances are identified, quarantine the lot, initiate corrective action, and repeat FAI after resolution.

Rationale and examples
13. Rationale
   13.1 Holding the billet at a documented target temperature in EQ-P1-L2-IH02 is critical to material flow characteristics during rolling; deviation can cause geometry and microstructure variance. The target is documented in section 4.2 to ensure reproducibility.  
   13.2 Using the specified lubricant CFW-LUB-961 on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 ensures consistent frictional conditions and tool life; lubricant substitution alters boundary conditions and invalidates FAI results.

14. Examples
   14.1 Example acceptable outcome: dimensional readings within drawing limits, microstructure showing expected grain flow, and process logs showing stable temperature at the target in section 4.2 with continuous lubricant flow of CFW-LUB-961.  
   14.2 Example rejection cause: measured OD out of tolerance correlating with documented billet temperature below the target in section 4.2 during rolling.

Records to keep
15. Mandatory records for the FAI package:
   15.1 Completed FAI data sheet with all dimensional readings.  
   15.2 Process logs from EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and EQ-P1-L2-RR01 showing temperature and machine state.  
   15.3 Material certificate and heat number traceability.  
   15.4 Lubricant batch label showing CFW-LUB-961 and maintenance acceptance from MM-P1-L2-RR01.  
   15.5 Calibration certificates for measurement instruments.  
   15.6 Photographic record of part surfaces and setup.  
   15.7 Any nonconformance reports and corrective action documentation.

Related documents
16. Reference documents: MM-P1-L2-IH02, MM-P1-L2-RR01, MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1.

Sign-off
17. Acceptance sign-off. The FAI package must be reviewed and signed by: production lead, quality engineer, and process engineer. Record names, titles, and signatures in the FAI approval block. Failure to complete sign-off invalidates release into production.
